_metadata.description: Cipher manuscripts and coded writing systems from the Voynich's temporal-geographic zone (c.1350-1530, Northern Italy / Southern Germany / Austria / Alsace / Switzerland)
_metadata.relevance_scale: VERY_HIGH = same region + period + content domain; HIGH = 2 of 3 match; MEDIUM = 1 of 3 match + interesting parallel; LOW = contextual only

cipher_manuscripts.name: Alchymey Teuczsch

cipher_details.what_is_encrypted: alchemical formulas, gold multiplication procedures, transmutation recipes
cipher_details.what_is_clear: medical recipes, astrological calendar, magical spells/incantations, Cisioianus
cipher_details.encryption_logic: Only knowledge with commercial or competitive value is encrypted; general knowledge remains readable
cipher_details.cipher_key: Provided on fol. 1r, later struck through to prevent easy access
cipher_details.authors_statement: We ourselves created this new alphabet so that one would not recognize it as an alphabet
cipher_details.decknamen_layer: Additional word-level encoding beyond cipher: gold = gelbe Erde (yellow earth), silver = weisse Erde (white earth), saltpeter = Salzstein (salt stone)
cipher_details.vulnerability: Breakable via word endings (common German suffixes remain identifiable in cipher text)

cipher_manuscripts.predecessor_tradition: Likely successors to Jewish alchemist Salman Teublein (P038); manuscript binding is a diploma concerning Teublein's obligation to keep his art secret
voynich_parallels: Same geographic zone (Bavaria vs. Voynich radiocarbon provenance)
Same period (1426 vs. 1404-1438 radiocarbon)
Alchemical-pharmaceutical content domain
Multiple cipher alphabets (Voynich has no known alphabet)
German-language base text
Selective encryption of commercially valuable knowledge
Group authorship (3+ collaborators)
voynich_differences: Alchymey Teuczsch uses simple substitution (deciphered by Eis 1951); Voynich resists all decipherment
Alchymey Teuczsch has clear-text sections; Voynich is entirely in its script
Alchymey Teuczsch includes cipher key (fol. 1r, struck through); Voynich has no key
No botanical illustrations in Alchymey Teuczsch
Alchymey Teuczsch is paper; Voynich is vellum
key_references: Wattenbach, 'Alchymey teuczsch', Anzeiger fur Kunde der deutschen Vorzeit 16 (1869), cols. 264-268
Eis, 'Von der Rede und dem Schweigen der Alchemisten', Deutsche Vierteljahrsschrift 25 (1951), pp. 415-435
Bischoff, 'Ubersicht uber die nichtdiplomatischen Geheimschriften des Mittelalters', MIOG 62 (1954)
Rec, 'Ciphers and Secrecy Among the Alchemists', Societas Magica Newsletter 31 (2014), pp. 1-6
Rec, 'Jewish Alchemists in Central Europe', Speculum (c.2018)

cipher_manuscripts.name: Bellicorum instrumentorum liber (Giovanni Fontana)

cipher_details.what_is_clear: first sentence of each description in Latin
cipher_details.glyph_design: Invented signs — no letters or numbers used in cipher portions
cipher_details.difficulty: Relatively easy to read by design; suggests concealment from casual readers, not serious cryptographic security

voynich_parallels: Padua physician — exact institutional and geographic match
Exact radiocarbon overlap (c.1420 vs. 1404-1438)
Invented glyph system — not standard alphabet substitution
Selective encryption pattern (clear text + cipher text mixed)
Technical/scientific content domain
Fontana held both arts and medical degrees from Padua
voynich_differences: Fontana's cipher is simple substitution (decipherable); Voynich is not
Fontana's cipher was designed to be relatively easy to read
Fontana's subject matter is military/technical, not botanical/pharmaceutical
Fontana provides Latin clear-text headers; Voynich has no clear text
key_references: Battisti & Saccaro Battisti, Le macchine cifrate di Giovanni Fontana (1984)

cipher_manuscripts.name: Secretum de thesauro experimentorum ymaginationis hominum (Giovanni Fontana)
voynich_parallels: Same author as CP002 — establishes a pattern of cipher use by a Padua physician
Mnemonic/memory system content — connects to knowledge organization
Title includes 'Secretum' — explicit secrecy framing

cipher_manuscripts.name: Buch der heiligen Dreifaltigkeit

cipher_details.encryption_logic: Cipher grids appear within an allegorical framework (alchemical process = Passion of Christ); first alchemical text in German

voynich_parallels: Southern Germany/Austria origin — same region
Exact period overlap (1410-1419 vs. 1404-1438)
Alchemical content with cipher elements
German-language base text
Franciscan authorship — mendicant order with alchemical interests
voynich_differences: Primarily allegorical rather than systematic cipher
Cipher grids are limited elements within larger clear text

cipher_manuscripts.name: Mellon MS 27 (Alchemical Miscellany)
cipher_manuscripts.shelfmark: New Haven, Yale, Beinecke Library, Mellon MS 27
voynich_parallels: German-speaking origin, 15th century
Same repository as Voynich (Beinecke Library)
Selective encryption of alchemical content
Multiple scribal hands — collaborative/accumulated knowledge
Mix of medical and alchemical recipes

cipher_manuscripts.name: Tranchedino Cipher Ledger
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: ~300 cipher keys: homophones, nomenclators, nulls, syllable substitutions

cipher_details.context: Working reference manual for the Sforza chancellery's diplomatic encryption

voynich_parallels: Now held in Vienna (ONB) — same library as many Voynich-era manuscripts
Demonstrates sophisticated Northern Italian cipher culture during Voynich period
The Milanese system was the most advanced in Europe by 1450
key_references: Springer: Deciphering the Diplomatic Archives of 15th-C Italy

cipher_manuscripts.name: Gabriele de Lavinde Papal Ciphers
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: first documented nomenclator: monoalphabetic substitution + nulls + two-letter word codes

cipher_details.innovation: First documented nomenclator system in European history

voynich_parallels: Avignon connection — same city where Rupescissa wrote (imprisoned)
Predates Voynich by ~25-50 years; establishes that cipher was routine in papal circles
Shows cipher culture was embedded in the same institutional networks as alchemical knowledge

cipher_manuscripts.name: Mantua Homophonic Cipher (Francesco I Gonzaga)

cipher_details.method: Reversed alphabet (A→Z, B→Y, etc.) + multiple homophonic shapes per vowel (~4 each)
cipher_details.correspondents: Simeone de Crema, King of Hungary

voynich_parallels: Northern Italy, exact radiocarbon overlap (1401 vs. 1404-1438)
Earliest homophonic substitution — relevant to Voynich entropy properties
Gonzaga connection to Hungarian court (King of Hungary) — later Voynich provenance touches Hungary

cipher_manuscripts.name: Paolo Guinigi Cipher Archive
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: mixed characters, letters, numbers; includes 'Greek alphabet' key

cipher_details.features: Artistically inventive cipher key designs; monoalphabetic with nomenclature
cipher_details.notable: Greek alphabet key shared with Antonio de Giglis

cipher_manuscripts.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Lucca, Governo da Paolo Guinigi, Codex No. 5
voynich_parallels: 74 keys from 1401-1439 — exact Voynich period
Earliest enciphered letters from 1404 — exact radiocarbon start date
Artistically inventive glyph designs (not just letter substitution)
Italian city-state context
key_references: Cipher Mysteries: Paolo Guinigi and Ciphers (Pelling, 2020)

cipher_manuscripts.name: Cicco Simonetta, Regulae ad extrahendum
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: not a cipher — first European cryptanalysis manual

cipher_details.methods: Vowel identification, common short word patterns, q-u digraph rule
cipher_details.note: Does NOT include frequency analysis — that comes later

voynich_parallels: Demonstrates that by 1474, cipher-breaking was a recognized professional skill in Northern Italy
If the Voynich was created in this environment, its creator may have been aware of cryptanalysis and designed accordingly

cipher_manuscripts.name: Leon Battista Alberti, De componendis cifris
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: first Western cryptography treatise; polyalphabetic substitution; cipher disk

cipher_details.innovation: Alberti Cipher Disk — two concentric rotating disks implementing polyalphabetic substitution with mixed alphabets
cipher_details.note: Circulated as manuscript until first printing 1568

voynich_parallels: Italian intellectual context
Polyalphabetic substitution — relevant to Voynich statistical properties
Manuscript circulation only until 1568 — knowledge was restricted

cipher_manuscripts.name: Johannes Trithemius, Steganographia
cipher_manuscripts.content_type: cryptographic/steganographic treatise disguised as angel magic

cipher_details.structure: Books I-II disguise cipher as angel-summoning rituals; Book III also contains cryptographic material (proven by Jim Reeds, 1998)
cipher_details.cultural_significance: First book-length treatment of cryptography; deliberately disguised as occult text

voynich_parallels: German-speaking region
Deliberate disguise of cryptographic content as something else
Connects secrecy traditions to occult/magical framing
Influenced by earlier traditions including Bacon and Secretum Secretorum

cipher_manuscripts.name: Alchemical Decknamen tradition

cipher_details.method: Coded nomenclature — systematic pseudonyms for substances, processes, and the elixir
cipher_details.examples: Green lion = vitriol; red lion = cinnabar/mercury sulfide; etc.
cipher_details.distinction: Professional jargon and deliberate obfuscation, not letter-level cipher

voynich_parallels: Same knowledge domain (alchemical/pharmaceutical)
Demonstrates that concealment was NORMAL in this field
Word-level encoding rather than letter-level — potentially relevant to Voynich token structure
Commercially motivated secrecy (protect valuable formulas)
key_references: Lang, Situating Ciphers Among Alchemical Techniques of Secrecy (HistoCrypt)

cipher_manuscripts.name: Codex Rohonczi
cipher_manuscripts.shelfmark: Budapest, Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
voynich_parallels: Undeciphered manuscript with unknown script
Venetian paper connection
Austria-Hungary border zone
key_references: Benedek Lang, The Rohonc Code (Penn State UP, 2021)

cipher_manuscripts.name: Roger Bacon, Epistola de secretis operibus
cipher_manuscripts.cipher_type: theoretical — describes 7 methods of concealing knowledge

cipher_details.gunpowder_cipher: Contains alleged anagram concealing gunpowder recipe (disputed)
cipher_details.principle: Dangerous knowledge should be hidden from the vulgar but accessible to the wise

voynich_parallels: Bacon was historically associated with the Voynich (Wilfrid Voynich's original attribution)
His advocacy for concealment provided intellectual justification for 15th-C cipher traditions
His Secretum Secretorum edition (~600 Latin copies) established the cultural norm that important knowledge = secrets
Widely copied in the same manuscript collections as alchemical texts
key_references: Voynich Revisionist: Roger Bacon on Ciphers

cipher_manuscripts.name: Konrad Kyeser, Bellifortis

cipher_details.note: NOT enciphered, but first fully illustrated manual of military technology; includes occult/magical content alongside technical material; parallels Fontana's approach

voynich_parallels: Bavaria, exact period (1402-1405 vs. 1404-1438)
Mix of technical and occult knowledge in illustrated manuscript
Written in exile (parallels secrecy/concealment motivation)
Contemporary of Fontana — same intersection of technical/military/magical

synthesis.pattern_summary: The Voynich manuscript was created during a period of intense cipher activity in its geographic zone. Between 1379-1499, we can document cipher use in at least 4 distinct domains: (1) diplomatic correspondence (Italian city-states, papacy), (2) alchemical manuscripts (Bavaria, German-speaking lands), (3) technical/medical treatises (Padua/Venice), and (4) theoretical cryptography (Alberti, Trithemius). The alchemical tradition is most relevant to the Voynich because it shares the same content domain, geographic zone, and selective-encryption logic.
key_observations: SELECTIVE ENCRYPTION: Both the Alchymey Teuczsch and Fontana encrypt only the commercially/strategically valuable content, leaving general knowledge in clear text. The Voynich is entirely in its script — either everything was considered secret, or the system is not selective encryption.
INVENTED GLYPHS: Fontana and possibly others used invented signs rather than standard alphabet substitution. This is closer to the Voynich than simple letter-for-letter substitution.

DECKNAMEN vs CIPHER: The alchemical tradition used BOTH word-level encoding (Decknamen) and letter-level cipher. The Voynich's token structure (morphological regularity, limited MIDDLE vocabulary) may reflect word-level encoding rather than letter-level cipher.

COMMERCIAL MOTIVATION: The Alchymey Teuczsch selectively encrypts commercially valuable formulas. If the Voynich encodes distillation procedures (our working model), the same commercial motivation applies.
INSTITUTIONAL CONTEXT: Cipher use correlates with institutional power — diplomatic chanceries, university faculties, court physicians. The Voynich's author likely had institutional backing.

SECRECY-TO-OPENNESS TRANSITION: Brunschwig's 1512 'geoffenbart' (revealed) marks the moment when printed vernacular texts made formerly secret knowledge public. The Voynich may represent the pre-revelation period.
